clue.text: What a skilled craftsman should be able to make if he gets a job at the Mint?

definitions.text: What a skilled craftsman should be able to make if he gets a job at the Mint?

parts.words: What a skilled craftsman should be able to make if he gets a job at the Mint?
parts.note: a skilled worker earns a high wage, and at the Mint, where coins are struck, the worker would literally make sound cash

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a high wage; the Mint is the place that manufactures Britain's coins, so the craftsman there would literally make it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means high pay, and a Mint employee also manufactures genuine coins.

clue.text: Is admittedly possessive?

parts.note: the verb can mean to admit or confess (as in confessing to something) and also to possess

explanation.walkthrough: The verb has two senses: to possess, and to admit or confess something, as in owning up.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to hold as property and to confess, so it is admittedly possessive.

clue.text: Strange men in obscure part of Europe

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for obscure
strange suggests the letters of the word men are in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Odd men lurking in some shadowy corner of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges MEN to ENM, which goes 'in' DARK.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Scandinavian country, one region of the continent.

clue.text: Mail ready to go to a remote settlement?

explanation.definitionFit: Post that is out is mail sent off; a frontier station far from the centre is an outlying camp.

clue.text: A school bill that's rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters of the word are read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a bill is a banknote, a note

explanation.surface: Fees at a famous school keep going up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'that's rising' reads NOTE upwards. ETON is England's best-known private boarding school, near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Large sea-fish coming up river estuary on the coast of East Anglia

definitions.text: on the coast of East Anglia

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the fish's name is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a ray is a flat sea-fish
a river's estuary is its mouth

explanation.surface: A big fish swims upstream from the sea to an East Anglian estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' turns RAY into YAR, which is also the name of the river the town stands on. East Anglia is the region of eastern England made up of Norfolk and Suffolk; the definition describes a seaside town there.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Norfolk port and resort town on the eastern seaboard of England.

clue.text: What the child was christened?

parts.note: the name a child is given at a christening ceremony in church

explanation.definitionFit: A Christian name given at the font is the one a child receives when christened.

clue.text: Liverpool's biggest annual event of course

definitions.text: Liverpool's biggest annual event of course

parts.words: Liverpool's biggest annual event of course
parts.note: of course reads as 'naturally' but means on a racecourse: the famous steeplechase at Aintree, near Liverpool

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' seems to mean 'naturally' but means held on a racecourse: this is the steeplechase run every spring at Aintree, on the edge of Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the famous steeplechase horse race held each year at Aintree racecourse by Liverpool.

clue.text: Food for a banquet raised to encourage team effort?

explanation.definitionFit: Hearty fare is old-fashioned feasting; a loud shout of support raised for a side is a fine cheer.

clue.text: In luck's way at coming into a large sum of money

indicators.note: at comes into, that is goes inside, the word for a large sum

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone inheriting a pile of money is surely in luck.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface, 'coming into a large sum' reads as inheriting money; in the wordplay 'coming into' is the signal for one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky, blessed with good luck.

clue.text: A pilot emeer turning left at the jeweller's, maybe

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A pilot emeer turning left at the jeweller's, maybe': wordplay needs A + PO (pilot officer) turned + L (left); 'emeer' looks like an OCR garble of 'officer', more than 3 letters off, and no scan or search gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: A pilot emeer turning left at the jeweller's, maybe

clue.text: Joyous song composed by Lorca

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the poet's name is rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: A happy song written by the Spanish poet Lorca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed by' rearranges LORCA, the Spanish poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas-style festive hymn is a joyful song.

clue.text: Dry fellow in spectacles defining the scent of the rose

indicators.note: the teetotal letters sit inside the round glasses shape

parts.note: spectacles look like two Os, OO
a dry fellow is teetotal, TT

explanation.surface: A teetotaller in glasses describes the perfume of a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: TT means teetotal, i.e. 'dry'; OO pictures a pair of spectacles. Otto (or attar) of roses is the oil from rose petals.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar or otto of roses is the fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: A far from wholesome thing to vote in

parts.note: a voter marks the ballot with a cross, X

explanation.surface: Something unhealthy is what one might vote into office.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the cross put on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison is harmful rather than healthy.

clue.text: Capricious little child-minder?

parts.note: capricious hints at the Latin for goat, so a female goat shares its name with someone paid to mind children

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capricious' comes from Latin 'capra', goat: a she-goat is called by the same word as a children's nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's nurse shares the name of a female goat, the creature capricious points to.

clue.text: Sales record not suitable for bedside reading?

explanation.definitionFit: A daily ledger records transactions; a volume for daytime is not one for night reading in bed.

clue.text: Moving passage from "Tristan"

indicators.note: moving means the letters of the opera title are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A stirring extract from Wagner's opera Tristan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges TRISTAN; 'passage' reads like a passage of music but means a journey across.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing through or across, a journey from one place to another.

clue.text: Cross-country runner able to do a verticle take-off

definitions.text: able to do a verticle take-off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Verticle' is printed for 'vertical'. The second sense is the Harrier jump jet, a British warplane that takes off straight upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound or athlete running cross-country; also the British jump jet, which lifts off straight up.

clue.text: Monarch who achieved monumental fame at Abu Simbel

definitions.text: Monarch who achieved monumental fame at Abu Simbel

parts.words: Monarch who achieved monumental fame at Abu Simbel
parts.note: the Egyptian pharaoh whose giant seated statues front the rock temples of Abu Simbel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Monumental' is literal: the colossal statues at Abu Simbel in Egypt depict this pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: The great pharaoh of Egypt built the rock temples there.

clue.text: Hold I cannot break

indicators.note: break means the phrase I cannot is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they cannot break their hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' rearranges the letters of I CANNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold is to enclose or have within.

clue.text: Somerset town holding me under a spell

indicators.note: the town's name holds, that is contains, the word me

parts.note: Chard is a market town in Somerset

explanation.surface: A town in Somerset has bewitched me.
explanation.walkthrough: Chard is a small town in Somerset, a county in south-west England; 'holding' puts ME inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanted, bewitched by magic.

clue.text: Poetically dark wood that is hard to polish

definitions.text: wood that is hard to polish

explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for black; also a poetic name for ebony, a dense hardwood that takes a high shine.

clue.text: A slur on a slide subjected to microscopic examination, perhaps

definitions.text: a slide subjected to microscopic examination, perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: A defamatory attack on someone's name; also a sample spread on a glass slide for a microscope, as in a cervical test.

clue.text: Cross-grained little wading bird?

definitions.meaning: describes a hard lump in timber where the grain runs across

explanation.definitionFit: A whorl in timber where the grain twists; also a small sandpiper that wades on shores.

clue.text: A little trout for tea?

explanation.definitionFit: A small fish of the salmon family related to trout; also British slang for tea, from Chinese 'cha'.

clue.text: Bring about bewilderment by striking

parts.note: to knock someone senseless with a blow, leaving them dazed

explanation.definitionFit: To daze with a blow is to knock someone senseless.

clue.text: Nevertheless, when coincidences take place

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning however; also simultaneously, which is when coinciding events occur.

clue.text: He may well be the first man on board

definitions.text: He may well be the first man on board

parts.words: He may well be the first man on board
parts.note: on board suggests a ship but means a board of directors, headed by its chief officer

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests boarding a ship or plane but means a company's board of directors, whose chairman ranks first.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a company or board presides over it as top man.
